reported_by: claude (23-01 executor and execute-phase orchestrator, code re-read 2026-11-11)
title: HTTP anti-rug polling requests the whole outstanding range unchunked and resumes from the stored chain_state block after a restart, so a gap larger than the provider log-range limit (an ordinary few-minute outage or restart) fails every poll from then on while the chain reports connected

evidence.note: getLogs from lastBlock + 1 to current, no chunking

evidence.ref: sed -n 1279,1300p of the base snapshot (22-27 merge)
evidence.note: Claude verification: lines re-read. A failed poll leaves lastBlock unchanged, so the range only grows. Not reproduced against a provider.
the poller seeds lastBlock from the chain_state row when one exists (HEAD :1231-1235), so a restart resumes from the stuck block
the row also advances on a tick with no registered positions (HEAD :1272-1279); with a held position it does not
restart re-registers held positions (Step 3) before startChainAntiRugListener starts the poller (Step 4) (HEAD :2122-2146)
defaultAntiRugBackfillCapBlocks 10 on ETH, "Alchemy free-tier safe"; 500 on the other chains (:294, :351, :408)
HTTP polling sets healthState connected (HEAD :1245); a failed tick only logs antirug.http-polling.error (:1312, HEAD :1315)
line refs re-measured at the audit base and at HEAD; the 23-01 checkpoint cited bot.ts :2120-2144 as HEAD, which is the base range (HEAD is :2122-2146). Not reproduced against a provider.

sibling_sites_checked: Backfill uses a chunked helper (getLogsForBackfill) and TH-ANTIRUG-06 holds that cap. The HTTP poller does not use it. Re-read 2026-11-11: the first anti-rug start stamps the dry-run row before the poller seeds (detector.ts:585 at base, :588 at HEAD; AUD-ANTIRUG-024), so the poller's no-row seed branch is not taken after the stamp and its start block on a chain's first start is 0; this is harmless while no position is registered (the no-positions tick moves it to the head) and is noted here, not graded separately.
severity_rationale: S1 (raised from S2 on 2026-11-11 by operator ruling ESC-ANTIRUG-03). Capital can be stranded under a plausible condition: on a chain running without a WebSocket URL, a held position loses rug protection, silently, after an ordinary outage or restart. The S2 rationale rested on two sub-claims that a code re-read falsified. (a) "Protection then stays off until restart" is wrong: a restart does not clear it. The poller re-reads its start block from the chain_state row (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1228-1232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, :1231-1235 at HEAD), the row advances only after a successful poll (:1300-1306 at base, :1303-1309 at HEAD) or a tick with no registered positions (:1269-1276 at base, :1272-1279 at HEAD), and on restart the held positions are re-registered before the poller starts (src/bot.ts:2120-2144 at base, :2122-2146 at HEAD), so the first poll after a restart requests the whole downtime range again and fails the same way. (b) "after an outage larger than the provider range limit" understated how ordinary the condition is: getLogs asks for lastBlock+1..currentBlock in one call (:1279-1291 at base, :1282-1294 at HEAD), and the repo's own range assumption is 10 blocks on ETH ("Alchemy free-tier safe", src/chainRegistry.ts:223-230, unchanged at HEAD) and 500 on the other chains (:294, :351, :408), so about two minutes of downtime on ETH (10 blocks of 12 s) is enough. It is silent: the dashboard shows the chain connected (detector.ts:1242 at base, :1245 at HEAD; AUD-ANTIRUG-007) and the only signal is a repeating antirug.http-polling.error log line (:1312 at base, :1315 at HEAD). Not reproduced yet; whether the operator's provider refuses these ranges is unmeasured, and the operator does not know whether any chain runs without a WebSocket URL. The grade does not depend on that exposure. Phase 23 Wave 5 gives it a real-path test that fails today; the fix is a Phase 24 capital fix (card OD-48).
recommendation: Use the chunked helper in the poller and bound the catch-up so a long gap is replayed in provider-sized windows; surface a failed poll as a health change instead of reporting connected; decide the outage handling in card OD-48. Phase 24 (capital fix, S1 since ESC-ANTIRUG-03), after a Phase 23 Wave 5 real-path test that fails today. Nothing is fixed in Phase 22 or 23.

sub_claims.claim: (1) A restart does not clear the stuck range: the poller resumes from the stored chain_state block, which only advances after a successful poll or a no-positions tick, and held positions are registered before the poller starts.
(2) Ordinary downtime triggers it: getLogs requests lastBlock+1..currentBlock unchunked, and the repo assumes a 10-block range on ETH (about two minutes) and 500 blocks elsewhere.
sub_claims.status: confirmed (code reading); provider refusal of these ranges not measured

sub_claims.claim: (3) It is silent: HTTP polling reports the chain connected and a failed tick only logs antirug.http-polling.error and retries the same range.

severity_history.by: operator ruling at the 23-01 blocking checkpoint
